title: Compatibility stewardship for fallback variants (tokenizer/KV/tooling sweep)
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Maintain and reconcile the fallback-variant compatibility registry so runtime routing can safely fall back across regions and tiers without tokenizer/context/tooling regressions. Scope covers: tokenizer byte-level parity, KV cache context sizing and offsets, model-tooling CLI/serving flags, and automated gates exposed to Smart Routing policies. Deliverables: updated compatibility registry CSV, a regression suite for tokenizer/context mismatches, migration scripts to patch variant metadata, and updated telemetry signals for parity drift detection.

Why now: Increased incidents where canary -> fallback switches produced subtle decoding issues (off-by-one tokens) and KV cache mismatches causing context truncation. This work reduces customer-facing degradation during automated fallbacks and is a prerequisite for expanding multi-region tier routing.

Out of scope: retraining models, large-scale tokenizer retokenization across model zoo, on-prem installer changes (these handled by Private deployment sprint).
comments: 2026-03-02 — Kickoff: triage notes from ops; flagged top 12 fallback pairs with highest fallback rate. See initial audit: https://drive.redwood.ai/fallback-audit-2026-03-02.csv

2026-03-05 — Design review with Applied ML: decided to treat tokenizer encoding differences as first-class attributes in the registry rather than normalizing encoders at runtime. Trade-off: faster rollouts vs. added routing complexity.

2026-03-07 — Eng sync: Liam proposed an automated shim to detect off-by-one tokenization at response time and emit a parity_violation signal to telemetry. Action: prototype in runtime branch 'parity-signal/proto' (PR linked below).
2026-03-10 — PM feedback (Jordan Blake): prioritize pairs impacting hosted customers with >1000 requests/day; added to ticket dependency list.
runbook: Verification steps: 1) Run `tools/parity_check --pair modelA:modelB --sample 500` to assert tokenizer encode/decode equivalence; 2) Validate KV offsets via `runtime/debug/kv-offset-check --model modelB`; 3) Deploy canary with registry flag `parity-gated=true` and trigger fallback in staging; 4) Confirm no parity_violation events in telemetry for 30 minutes. Rollback plan: revert registry entries and promote pre-parity shim that prefers same-tokenizer fallbacks only.
acceptance_criteria: Registry updated with parity attributes (tokenizer_version, tokenizer_hash, kv_context_bytes, tooling_flags) for top 100 fallback pairs.
Automated regression job created: weekly run that validates tokenization and KV offsets and creates issues if drift detected.
Telemetry emits parity_violation events and an alert rule is in Grafana with severity and runbook link.
Smart Routing policies can reference registry attributes to avoid incompatible fallbacks (unit and integration tests green).
Migration script available and tested in staging to update legacy variant metadata; PR merged and documented.
